stem.en: Why is it inaccurate to say a pregnant person's maternal and fetal blood 'mix together' in the placenta to deliver oxygen and nutrients to the fetus?
stem.et: Miks on ebatäpne öelda, et raseda inimese ema ja loote veri 'seguneb' platsentas, et viia lootele hapnikku ja toitaineid?

label.en: Because maternal and fetal blood remain in separate circulations throughout pregnancy; exchange happens across a thin placental membrane separating the two closely apposed but distinct blood supplies, not through direct mixing.
label.et: Sest ema ja loote veri jäävad kogu raseduse ajaks eraldiseisvateks vereringeteks; vahetus toimub üle õhukese platsenta membraani, mis eraldab kahte tihedalt kõrvuti asetsevat, kuid eraldiseisvat verevarustust, mitte otsese segunemise kaudu.

label.en: Because the placenta is only maternal tissue extending from the uterine lining, so there was never a separate fetal blood supply to keep apart from the mother's in the first place.
label.et: Sest platsenta on ainult emaka limaskestast lähtuv ema kude, mistõttu ei olnudki kunagi eraldi loote verevarustust, mida ema omast lahus hoida.

label.en: Because oxygen and nutrient exchange is handled by the corpus luteum for the entire pregnancy, with the placenta's role limited only to hormone production.
label.et: Sest hapniku ja toitainete vahetust käsitleb kogu raseduse jooksul kollaskeha, ning platsenta roll piirdub ainult hormoonide tootmisega.

label.en: It isn't inaccurate -- maternal and fetal blood genuinely do mix directly within the placenta's shared vessels.
label.et: See ei ole ebatäpne -- ema ja loote veri tõesti seguneb otseselt platsenta jagatud veresoontes.
